questions.stem: Which set of assets would best support a claim that Zephyr Mattresses, a privately held firm has strong brand equity in Yewton?
questions.explanation: Brand equity rests on assets such as awareness, the strength and favourability of associations, and loyalty. These create durable value and willingness to pay. A large factory or wide distribution may support a business but is not brand equity, and heavy discounting can actually weaken a brand's perceived value over time.

questions.stem: After years of steady sales, Brightwater Kitchenware, a small firm sees its Fairhaven product's sales and profits begin to fall as newer alternatives appear. Which stage has the product entered?
questions.explanation: Falling sales and profits, driven by newer substitutes, define the decline stage. In maturity, sales level off and competition intensifies, but they do not trend downward over time. In growth, sales climb quickly. Recognising decline helps a firm decide whether to harvest, rejuvenate or retire the product.

questions.stem: Graystone Outdoor Gear, a family-owned firm plans to sell a product in Nettleford at $66 per unit. Variable cost is $13 per unit and fixed costs are $40,451. How many units must it sell to break even?
questions.explanation: Break-even volume equals fixed cost divided by contribution per unit, where contribution is price minus variable cost. Contribution here is $53, and $40,451 divided by that is about 764 units. Dividing by price alone or by variable cost alone ignores the true contribution, and adding variable cost to price overstates it. At the break-even point profit is zero.

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Eastvale Dairy, a privately held firm buys an item for $106 and sells it in Crestview for $160. What is the gross margin as a percentage of the selling price?
questions.explanation: Gross margin is gross profit divided by selling price. Gross profit is $54, and dividing by the $160 selling price gives 34 percent. The figure of 51 percent is the markup on cost, which uses cost as the denominator and is always larger. Mixing up margin and markup is a common pricing error that can badly understate the needed price.
